title: The Chick Webb years as the highlight of his career
summary: McRae calls building the Webb band and Ella's rise his greatest experience, a school that prepared him for everything after.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them

blocks.x: Well I think there was only one instance of all the things I was involved in. I think that was the one with the Chick Webb thing. I think that was the most -- Because, here's something that was growing -- that we started in '36 up till the time he passed and the year after I took over the band. It's something that you could see it growing -- you could see it coming up, you know. You could see it mushrooming, getting larger and better and better and better. Right up to the last time that we played the Paramount Theater -- the great date at the

Paramount Theater -- the band was really on its way and Ella was on top.
And we had worked so hard to put this together. This was the -- I think one of the highlights of my career in the music business for me.
Because from then -- Why I say that, from then on I could go out and do -- probably anything that I wanted to do.
I mean, like, when I went with Cab Calloway or went with Louie Armstrong, and the things I did with King and Joe Glaser, you know.
On the Swing Street with my sextet that Glaser booked -- with Art Tatum and (inaudible) Laumell Morgan.
These things was just like -- well this is what I've learned. I learned all these things, you know.
I went through the school. Like the guy say I come from the big tent.
It was so much involved with Chick, like a building process -- the things that I had to go through with him, the things that we did together, you

know. Like, I mean, when we put that band together. It was so much -- By the time you got to the end, if you didn't know anything about that, you can just forget about it, you know. I learned how to put things together and really do things, you know. Like, if something had to be done, I could do it. You know, like, he say, "Well, look, we wanna do so and so and so. Figure it out and let's put a show together." So when I went with Louie -- when I had to go in the Zanzibar, we put the whole show -- that big show on in one day. It's just something I had learned from the beginning working with Chick Webb. Because this was a fast moving thing. You know, two or three months we be here, and the next month we be moving up. We were moving all the time through '36 and through '37 and '38, you know. We wasn't making a lot of money, but we were really (inaudible).

I got a lot of experience working with him, because it was so many things that he --
Nobody saw them, but between him and I we know, you know, always give me -- (inaudible), "What do you think about this, what do you think about this?"

And they were things that really led up to his success. I mean, we were doing -- Just like Charlie (Bachanan) (inaudible) say, "Maybe this guy is good for the band. The band sounds different now, so and so. Just what Chick needed," you know.
But it was just so much that he had in mind what he wanted to do that had to be worked out.
If he didn't have no idea, he could never work them out. You had to be on your p's and q's with him.
